items.followUp: Name one type of radiation used in radiotherapy and state its effect on cancer cells.

rubric.why: Identifies the radiation or source used in radiotherapy.
rubric.description: Radiotherapy uses high-energy radiation, such as gamma rays from cobalt-60.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a suitable radiation or source.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of radiotherapy on the cancer.
rubric.description: The radiation destroys cancer cells or shrinks the tumour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing either effect.

modelAnswer: Radiotherapy treats cancer by directing high-energy radiation, such as gamma rays from cobalt-60, at the cancerous area.
The radiation destroys cancer cells or shrinks the tumour.

items.followUp: How does atomic size change down a group, and why does this make it easier to remove an outer electron?

rubric.why: States the direction of the ionization-energy trend.
rubric.description: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the correct trend.

rubric.why: Explains why less energy is needed to remove an electron down a group.
rubric.description: The outer electron is farther from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is easier to remove.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased atomic radius, shielding, or distance from the nucleus to easier removal.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.
Atomic radius and shielding increase, so the outer electron is farther from the nucleus and easier to remove.

items.followUp: Why are the d-block elements placed in the main body of the periodic table?

rubric.why: Identifies the block or period placement of these elements.
rubric.description: Lanthanides and actinides are f-block elements belonging to periods 6 and 7, respectively.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the f-block or either series' period.

rubric.why: Explains the layout reason for showing these series separately.
rubric.description: They are shown separately below the main table to keep it compact and avoid making it too wide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the arrangement keeps the table compact or avoids excessive width.

modelAnswer: Lanthanides and actinides are f-block elements belonging to periods 6 and 7, respectively.
They are shown separately below the periodic table to keep it compact and avoid making it too wide.

items.followUp: What does δ− mean in a polar covalent bond, and how does it form?

rubric.why: Explains what the delta sign represents.
rubric.description: The delta sign (δ) indicates a partial charge; δ+ is partial positive and δ− is partial negative.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the delta sign as indicating a partial charge.

rubric.why: Explains how partial charges develop in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: A difference in electronegativity causes unequal sharing of electrons, producing partial charges.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking unequal sharing of electrons to electronegativity.

modelAnswer: The delta sign (δ) represents a partial charge: δ+ is partial positive and δ− is partial negative.
A difference in electronegativity causes unequal sharing of electrons in a polar covalent bond.
